heading: 3. Resolution Varies 3.5-fold Across Organisms

text: Resolution varied substantially by organism; links to reference annotation, coverage, and phylogenetic distance are the report's interpretations, not controlled tests.

Organisms with better-annotated reference genomes and stronger Fitness Browser coverage showed higher resolution rates. *B. thetaiotaomicron* — a Bacteroidetes with more divergent metabolism — had the lowest resolution, consistent with its phylogenetic distance from the proteobacterial majority.

text: Candidate assignments for rxn02185 and rxn03436, sequential branched-chain amino-acid biosynthesis steps, were each high-confidence in 9 of 14 organisms. Co-resolution is not independent experimental validation.
quote: The reactions rxn02185 (2-acetolactate pyruvate-lyase, EC 2.2.1.6, branched-chain amino acid biosynthesis) and rxn03436 (acetohydroxy acid isomeroreductase, EC 1.1.1.86, valine/isoleucine biosynthesis) were each resolved with high confidence in 9 of 14 organisms. These enzymes catalyze sequential steps in the same biosynthetic pathway, and their consistent co-resolution validates the triangulation approach — when one pathway gene is found, the adjacent step's gene is typically recoverable.
heading: 4. Two Reactions Dominate High-Confidence Assignments

heading: 5. "Dark Reactions" Resist Resolution

text: EC-less “dark reactions” comprised 50 of 201 (24.9%) and had 8 of 50 (16%) resolution, versus 88 of 151 (58.3%) for reactions with known EC numbers.
quote: Of 201 gapfilled reactions, 50 (24.9%) had no EC number assigned by ModelSEED ("dark reactions"). Only 8 of these 50 (16%) were resolved, compared to 88 of 151 (58.3%) for reactions with known EC numbers. Dark reactions represent the hardest annotation gaps — their functions are known only by stoichiometry, not by enzyme classification, making both sequence homology searches and functional annotation cross-referencing far more difficult.
heading: 5. "Dark Reactions" Resist Resolution

text: The report labels baseline flux balance analysis across 574 combinations as 42.5% overall accuracy, gives recall as 86.5% (244 of 282) and precision as 42.5% (244 of 574), and reports 330 false positives. The repeated accuracy and precision value should not be silently treated as independently verified metrics.
quote: Baseline FBA across 574 organism-carbon source combinations yielded 42.5% overall accuracy — but this masks asymmetric performance: recall (sensitivity) was 86.5% (244 of 282 growth-positive conditions correctly predicted), while precision was only 42.5% (244 of 574 growth predictions were correct) due to 330 false positives from overly permissive draft models.
heading: Study Design

text: The report states that gapfilling 38 false negatives added 219 reactions, averaging 5.8 per case, but its listed categories (201 enzymatic, 14 transport, 12 exchange) sum to 227; this numerical conflict remains unresolved.
quote: Conditional gapfilling on 38 false-negative cases (observed growth, predicted no-growth) added 219 reactions (201 enzymatic, 14 transport, 12 exchange), averaging 5.8 reactions per case.
heading: Study Design

text: EC-based matching via pangenome clusters resolved 51/201 pairs (25.4%) and generated 107 gene candidates.
quote: 1. **NB03 — EC-based matching**: Matched gapfilled reaction EC numbers to Fitness Browser gene annotations via pangenome gene clusters. Resolved 51/201 pairs (25.4%) with 107 gene candidates.
heading: Evidence Integration Pipeline

text: The Bakta alternative-annotation step reports 22 newly resolved pairs (10.9%) and 1,459 EC candidate entries; keep this step-level figure distinct from the single-stream comparison.
quote: 2. **NB04 — Bakta alternative annotations**: Queried Bakta annotations for alternative EC numbers and product-name matches for dark reactions. Added 22 newly resolved pairs (10.9%), yielding 1,459 Bakta EC candidate entries.
heading: Evidence Integration Pipeline

text: Pangenome fitness profiling covered 57 ECs across 14 organisms and reported 11 strong co-occurrence cases and four carbon-source-specific fitness defects.
quote: 3. **NB05 — Pangenome fitness profiling**: Built cross-organism EC presence/absence matrix (57 ECs x 14 organisms), computed fitness specificity z-scores, and identified 11 strong co-occurrence cases. Four carbon-source-specific fitness defects were found.
heading: Evidence Integration Pipeline

text: The NB06 pipeline passage instead says DIAMOND BLAST searched concatenated proteomes using 328 downloaded Swiss-Prot exemplars. The report leaves the search direction inconsistent with its Key Findings passage; both descriptions report 154 hits.
quote: 4. **NB06 — BLAST triangulation**: Downloaded 328 Swiss-Prot exemplar sequences for 75/84 unique ECs. DIAMOND BLAST against concatenated proteomes yielded 154 hits. Evidence triangulation with confidence scoring produced the final 96 resolved pairs (47.8%).
heading: Evidence Integration Pipeline

text: Although 23 gene–protein–reaction rules were inserted, simulated knockouts could not validate candidates: the wild-type models showed zero growth on the relevant minimal media without gapfilled reactions.
quote: 5. **NB07 — Validation**: Inserted 23 GPR rules into SBML models for high/medium-confidence NB03 candidates. Gene knockout simulation showed zero wildtype growth on minimal carbon source media — an expected limitation because the models require the gapfilled reactions themselves to enable growth on those carbon sources.
heading: Evidence Integration Pipeline

text: As reported in this project's literature context, Price et al. (2022) used mutant fitness data to annotate 716 proteins across diverse bacteria; this is attributed prior work, not a result of this project.
quote: Price et al. (2022, *PLoS Genetics*) used mutant fitness data to fill gaps in bacterial catabolic pathways, annotating 716 proteins across diverse bacteria.
heading: Literature Context

text: The report attributes likelihood-based, sequence-homology-guided gap-filling annotations and improved model quality to Benedict et al. (2014).
quote: Benedict et al. (2014, *PLoS Comput Biol*) developed likelihood-based gene annotations for gap filling using sequence homology, demonstrating that probabilistic approaches improve metabolic model quality.
heading: Literature Context

text: The report identifies gapseq as a methodological comparator using curated pathways and informed gap-filling, but distinguishes its model-reconstruction focus and lack of transposon-fitness integration.
quote: The gapseq tool (Zimmermann et al. 2021, *Genome Biology*, [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1186/s13059-021-02295-1)) represents the closest methodological comparator — it uses curated pathway databases and informed gap-filling to build metabolic models. However, gapseq focuses on model reconstruction rather than post-hoc resolution of annotation gaps, and does not integrate transposon fitness data.
heading: Literature Context

text: According to the report's PubMed attribution, Borchert et al. (2024) identified 84 functional gene modules from Pseudomonas putida RB-TnSeq data using independent component analysis; this is attributed prior work.
quote: According to PubMed, Borchert et al. (2024, *mSystems*, [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1128/msystems.00942-23)) applied independent component analysis to RB-TnSeq fitness data from *Pseudomonas putida*, identifying 84 functional gene modules.
heading: Literature Context

text: According to the report's PubMed attribution, Wetmore et al. (2015) performed 387 genome-wide fitness assays across 5 bacteria and identified 5,196 genes with significant phenotypes; these are prior-work figures.
quote: According to PubMed, the RB-TnSeq method itself was established by Wetmore et al. (2015, *mBio*, [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1128/mBio.00306-15)), who performed 387 genome-wide fitness assays across 5 bacteria and identified 5,196 genes with significant phenotypes.
heading: Literature Context

text: The report states that the Fitness Browser database covered 48 organisms at the time described; this is a report-era coverage figure.
quote: Our study leverages the Fitness Browser database that grew from this initial work, now covering 48 organisms.
heading: Literature Context

text: Automated draft-model errors and false-positive growth predictions limit interpretation of the reported 42.5% baseline FBA result.
quote: 1. **Model quality**: Draft models built from automated RAST annotations contain systematic errors. The 42.5% baseline FBA accuracy (dominated by false positives) reflects overly permissive models that predict growth on carbon sources the organisms cannot use
heading: Limitations

text: A minimum-reaction ModelSEED gapfill is not necessarily biologically correct; alternative valid solutions may exist.
quote: 2. **Gapfilling non-uniqueness**: Multiple valid gapfill solutions may exist for each false-negative case. We used the default ModelSEED gapfilling, which minimizes the number of added reactions but does not guarantee biological optimality
heading: Limitations

text: Manual mapping of 109 carbon sources to compound IDs is an error-sensitive step that could introduce spurious false negatives.
quote: 3. **Carbon source mapping**: The mapping between Fitness Browser experiment condition names and ModelSEED exchange reactions relied on manual curation (109 carbon sources mapped to compound IDs). Errors in this mapping would produce spurious false negatives
heading: Limitations

text: Fitness support depends on the chosen absolute-fitness threshold and experiment count; sparsely assayed organisms have less statistical power.
quote: 4. **Fitness threshold sensitivity**: Gene fitness significance depends on the chosen |fitness| threshold and number of experiments. Organisms with fewer carbon source experiments have less statistical power
heading: Limitations

text: GapMind covers ~80 carbon and amino-acid pathways rather than all metabolism, limiting corroboration of gapfilled reactions outside that scope.
quote: 5. **GapMind scope**: GapMind covers ~80 carbon and amino acid pathways, not full metabolism. Many gapfilled reactions fall outside GapMind's pathway coverage
heading: Limitations

text: The FBA knockout test was inconclusive and circular because the un-gapfilled models did not grow on the tested minimal media.
quote: 6. **Gene knockout simulation**: The FBA knockout validation was inconclusive because the models cannot grow on carbon source minimal media without the gapfilled reactions — the gapfilled reactions are themselves required to enable growth, making single-gene knockout analysis circular in this context
heading: Limitations

text: The sample was dominated by Proteobacteria (12 of 14); lower performance in the sole Bacteroidetes organism is only single-organism evidence for weaker transfer to distant clades.
quote: 7. **Phylogenetic bias**: 12 of 14 organisms are Proteobacteria, limiting generalizability. The sole Bacteroidetes (*B. thetaiotaomicron*) had the lowest resolution rate, suggesting the approach may be less effective for phylogenetically distant clades with divergent metabolism
heading: Limitations
